Two freehold Camden Park bungalow plots for sale at $26 mil and $27 mil
article:
Two adjacent freehold sites in the Camden Park Good Class Bungalow (GCB) area are being offered for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The residential sites, which each house a single-storey detached bungalow, are located at 15 and 15A Camden Park.

The sites are held under separate titles by the same owner, and are being offered for sale individually, marketing agent CBRE said in a Nov 10 release. Offers may be submitted for either property or for both.

The site at 15 Camden Park spans a land area of 13,116 sq ft and has a guide price of $26 million, or $1,982 psf. The site at 15A Camden Park measures 14,060 sq ft and is priced at $27 million, or $1,920 psf.

Each plot could potentially be redeveloped into “a substantial family residence”, said Rowena Chan, senior vice president of residential capital markets, Singapore at CBRE.

“Their adjoining location also provides an additional option for buyers seeking a larger landholding or wishing to establish neighbouring family homes,” she added.

Subject to prevailing planning requirements, site conditions and relevant approvals, the adjoining titles may be acquired together as a combined 27,176 sq ft holding.

According to CBRE, the properties were formerly the residence of the late Earnest Lau and Kwa Geok Lian.

Located in the Camden Park landed residential enclave in Bukit Timah, the sites are less than 1km from the Singapore Botanic Gardens, while the Botanic Gardens MRT Interchange (serving the Circle and Downtown lines) is also within walking distance.

The Camden Park area has 26 homes, with landholdings in the enclave averaging at approximately 22,605 sq ft, said CBRE.

As such, the properties at 15 and 15A Camden Park each offer “the prestige and privacy of a GCB area address at a more manageable overall investment quantum”, the firm added.

Caveats lodged show that the most recent transaction in Camden Park was for a detached house on a 29,922 sq ft freehold plot that fetched $48 million ($1,604 psf) in November 2025.

Before that, the last transaction occurred in September 2021, when a freehold detached home occupying a 16,607 sq ft site changed hands for $32.5 million ($1,957 psf).

The EOI will close at 5pm on Jan 20, 2027.

title: Tampines Mall completes $24 mil asset enhancement initiative
article:
Tampines Mall is completing its $24 million asset enhancement initiative (AEI) in December, marking a new chapter for the eight-storey shopping centre in the Tampines Regional Centre.

The mall, owned by CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT), began the AEI in September 2025 to improve about 50,000 sq ft of net lettable area.

In its 3Q2026 financial update, published on Oct 29, CICT said around 97% of the AEI space is committed or in advanced negotiation as of Sept 30.

In a separate Nov 10 release, Tampines Mall said the transformation introduces 21 new brands, including 15 making their debut in the East. The mall now houses over 160 stores, with a net lettable area exceeding 356,000 sq ft.

“The refreshed Tampines Mall brings together a broad mix of premium, accessible-luxury and everyday brands, alongside dining, sports and lifestyle offerings and well-loved favourites,” added Adrian Lai, general manager of Tampines Mall.

A highlight of the revamped mall is a beauty cluster with 14 brands, including Sephora.

The beauty retailer, which previously operated at neighbouring shopping centre Tampines 1 now occupies ground-floor space that was formerly part of Isetan. The Japanese department store closed its Tampines Mall outlet in November 2025 after 30 years.

Other brands in the beauty cluster include new-to-Tampines Mall names such as British skincare brand Elemis, Chinese makeup retailer Judydoll, Dutch home and body cosmetics brand Rituals, as well as luxury brand YSL Beauty.

In addition, beauty brands such as Shiseido and Chanel, which previously operated through store concessions within Isetan, have opened standalone boutiques in the mall.

Another highlight of the AEI is a refresh of the dining line-up at Tampinese Mall. New additions include Italian dining concept Casa Vostra, Chinese milk tea brand Charlie’s Tea, Hong Kong-founded Ging Sun Ho King of Bun and specialty coffee shop Alchemist.

The mall has also expanded its jewellery and fashion offerings. Key changes include Decathlon, which closed their click-and-collect store at Tampines Mall at the start of the year. The French sports retailer is moving into a more spacious 18,000 sq ft store on Level 2 that will open in December.

Other new names include German leather goods store Braun Büffel, international fashion brand Meilleur Moment, watch dealer Vincent Watch and travel accessories store Boarding Gate.

Tampines Mall first opened in 1995. It is adjacent to the Tampines MRT interchange (serving the East-West and Downtown lines) and the Tampines Bus Interchange. It also neighbours two other malls, Century Square and Tampines 1, which are both owned by Frasers Centrepoint Trust.

title: Could mortgage rates rise further? What bank packages in Singapore are signalling after Fed hike
article:
On Sept 16, the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. Within days, Singapore banks pulled their fixed-rate packages, repriced them outside their usual schedule, and brought them back at higher rates.

So, will rates keep rising? No one can say for sure, but today’s bank packages offer a useful clue.

What bank packages are telling us

When a bank fixes your rate, it locks in its own funding cost for the same period.

What that costs depends on where the market expects Sora — the key interest rate benchmark for floating-rate home loans in Singapore — to go.

That’s why the difference between a bank’s three-year and two-year fixed rates, known as the spread, is worth watching.

If banks expect rates to rise, fixing for three years costs them more, so the three-year rate is priced higher and the spread widens. If they expect rates to stay stable, the spread stays narrow. And if they expect rates to fall, the three-year rate can even come in cheaper than the two-year rate.

Fixed rates have risen by 0.30–0.77 percentage points (refer to Table 1). For most home loans, the three-year rate is now slightly above the two-year rate. The exception is the $300,000 HDB loan, where the three-year rate is cheaper.

Things get more interesting, however, when we look at how the spreads have changed.

As Table 2 shows, the gap between three-year and two-year rates has narrowed for half of the packages. Where the spread has widened, the increase is small, at 0.12 percentage point or less.

This may indicate that rates could stay at this level for now or mildly rise, rather than climb sharply.

What the Fed is signalling

After raising rates in September, the Fed held them steady at its October meeting, but its latest statement leaves the door open to another rise.

About 76% of experts expect one more hike before the end of the year, according to CNBC's latest Fed Survey of fund managers, strategists and economists.

If that happens, expect the same pattern in Singapore as the previous time: Sora will likely move first. Whether fixed rates follow depends on how much of a higher Sora banks have already priced in.

Fixed rates are up 0.30 to 0.77 percentage points, and with the spread narrowing for half of the packages. This could indicate that banks expect rates to stay stable or rise only modestly from here.

These are indicators, not predictions. Fed projections can shift quickly, and banks can reprice their packages at any time. Treat this as context for your own decision rather than financial advice.

What has happened since the Fed hike

1. Sora moved before the Fed did.

Sora is the average rate banks charge each other to borrow Singapore dollars overnight, and most floating home loans are pegged to it.

Singapore rates tend to follow US rates because money moves freely in and out of the country, though the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s management of the Singapore dollar, and factors like large capital inflows, soften the link.

Banks also price in what they expect, so Sora started drifting up months before the Fed moved.

The monthly average Sora went from about 1.00% in April to 1.27% in August, and averaged about 1.34% in October. On a $500,000 floating loan, a 0.27 percentage point rise works out to roughly $110 a month more in interest in the early years.

2. Floating loans are still catching up.

Most floating loans use the three-month Sora — an average of daily Sora over the past three months — so it catches up with the daily rate slowly.

The three-month Sora hit a low of 1.02% on 29 April, was 1.20% the day before the Fed's announcement, and has reached 1.32% as at the time of writing (based on data as at Nov 9), 55 days later. If your loan is pegged to it, you're likely paying for the summer rise with a delay.

Singapore benchmark rates: Daily Sora and three-month compounded Sora:

3. Fixed packages were pulled, then repriced.

A fixed rate is a commitment: once it is agreed, the bank is stuck with it, even if its own costs rise.

So, after the Fed's move on Sept 16, banks withdrew packages first and repriced them after (see Table 3), according to Cashew’s internal bank package data.

What this could mean for you

• If you're on a three-month Sora floating loan, expect the lag. The rise in the daily Sora is still feeding through the three-month average. Your rate won't jump sharply, but it may keep inching up for a few months, even if the headlines go quiet.

• If you're shopping for a fixed rate, treat pre-September rates as out of date. Packages have already been repriced higher, and many ads are still showing old rates.

• A rate isn't yours until it's approved. Packages are first come, first served, and they can change while your application waits in the queue.

• Don't panic. Over the life of your loan, rates will go up and down many times. If you switch to the lowest rate whenever your lock-in ends, you shouldn't overpay in the long run. You can do that by repricing (moving to a new package with your current bank) or refinancing (moving your loan to another bank)

The Fed’s September hike has already reshaped the market. Banks have repriced already, and Sora is still catching up.

But today's bank packages suggest rates may hold steady or rise only mildly from here, rather than climb sharply.

Whether you’re on a floating rate, coming to the end of a lock-in period, or buying your first home, what matters most is acting on current rates, not old ones. Compare your options early and make sure you’re on the lowest package available to you.

title: 3 US Stocks Down 30% – Are They Worth a Look?
article:
As tech leaders fall sharply from their peaks, investors are split on what to do next.
Some see it as a long-awaited Wall Street sale to grab a piece of these
tech titans
on the cheap.
Others contemplate a possible value trap.
Three technology leaders –
Alphabet Inc.
(NASDAQ: GOOGL),
Fortinet Inc.
(NASDAQ: FTNT), and
Broadcom Inc.
(NASDAQ: AVGO) – have seen roughly 30% of their equity values wiped out from the recent pullbacks.
Let’s unpack the insights behind their massive stock rout.
Alphabet: Capex Anxiety Meets Cloud Growth
Alphabet’s share price pulled back sharply from its peak of more than US$400 in May 2026 to around US$280, wiping out close to one-third of its market capitalisation.
The catalyst?
Earnings per share (EPS) missed in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026), coming in at US$2.12 against consensus analyst estimates of US$3.02.
As Alphabet owns a stake in the publicly listed SpaceX, a fall in the share price of the latter caused a non-operating accounting loss of US$8.7 billion for the quarter, which weighed on the bottom line.
Furthermore, Alphabet’s heavy capital outlays spooked investors, as it announced 3Q2026 quarterly capex of US$51.4 billion, pushing its free cash flow (FCF) to negative US$9.1 billion.
Although Alphabet’s 2026 capex is expected to stay within the guided range of US$195 billion to US$205 billion, capex spending in 2027 is projected to increase significantly, fuelling investors’ concerns.
However, Alphabet’s operating engines remain strong.
Its 3Q2026 revenue surged 25% year on year (YoY) to US$127.6 billion, driven by Google Cloud, which climbed 103% to US$30.7 billion.
Meanwhile, operating income increased 30% YoY to US$40.58 billion, with the operating margin improving from 31% to 32%, demonstrating improving operating leverage.
Right now, the market is offering Alphabet’s shares at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 13x – a significant discount relative to its
Magnificent Seven
peers, which trade at a median P/E of 31.6x.
Fortinet: Bottom-line Momentum Persists Despite Rising Costs
Fortinet share price has fallen around 30% despite the global cybersecurity company’s 3Q2026 revenue expanding 20% YoY to US$2.08 billion.
The revenue growth was driven by a 37% surge in product revenue to US$765 million, anchored by the growth in secure networking hardware and term licences.
Meanwhile, service revenue grew 13% to US$1.31 billion as the revenue for FortiGuard and other security subscription services was recognised.
Crucially, total gross margin contracted 1.8 percentage points to 79% as Fortinet shifts towards lower-margin product revenue, with the margin compression worsened by rising costs of memory chips and inventory-related expenses.
Moreover, although Fortinet is winning massive enterprise clients, these clients typically activate their services in phases, meaning the revenue is realised more slowly, exerting top-line pressure on Fortinet.
Still, Fortinet’s bottom-line momentum remains strong.
Its 3Q2026 operating income surged 29% to US$704.3 million and it delivered US$864.8 million in FCF. Fortinet demonstrated strong operating leverage as its top-line growth outpaced expense growth.
The verdict?
The latest sell-off reflects short-term market anxieties, rather than a structural decline of Fortinet’s business.
Broadcom: Valuation Reset vs Custom AI Dominance
From a peak of around US$490, Broadcom’s share price has dropped more than 30% to about US$330 per share, resetting its trailing P/E from over 70 to a more palatable level of over 40.
Still, investors should not ignore the custom chip designer’s concentration risk, with direct sales to one distributor accounting for 50% of its 3Q2026 net revenue.
In addition, its top five end customers account for approximately 55% of 3QFY2026 net revenue.
Despite these concentration risks, Broadcom remains dominant in custom chip design.
Revenue for its AI-driven Semiconductor Solutions segment skyrocketed 127% YoY to US$20.8 billion, lifting consolidated 3Q2026 revenue 85.5% YoY to US$29.59 billion, with an operating margin of 53.9%.
Backed by long-term demand from Big Tech firms such as Alphabet, Broadcom’s AI-led growth is expected to continue to 2031.
Crucially, Broadcom’s business is cash generative.
In the nine months ended 2 August 2026 (9MFY2026), Broadcom’s FCF increased 64.2% YoY to $31.9 billion – a stark contrast to hyperscalers alarming negative FCF.
The current valuation reset of a
cash-rich business
like Broadcom may make it worth a closer look for long-term investors.

It’s easy to succumb to myopic market noise and lose sight of durable businesses that compound in value over time.

title: 3 SGX Hidden Gems That Grew Profits by 24% (or More!)
article:
If you follow earnings season, you’ll know
blue chips
tend to hog the spotlight.
This time, some of the biggest profit gains came from much smaller companies.
Three Singapore-listed
small caps
grew their profits by 24% or more, and one more than doubled its bottom line.
If you invest for dividends, profit growth is a good start.
The cash behind it matters more.
One thing to keep in mind as you read: the three report over different periods, so watch the labels.
Can Tiong Woon keep raising its dividend?
Tiong Woon Corporation Holding Ltd
(SGX: BQM) is a one-stop integrated heavy-lift specialist with a presence in 12 countries.
Crane and transport hire makes up 96% of revenue.
For the financial year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), revenue rose 15% year on year (YoY) to S$187.7 million.
Profit attributable to shareholders climbed 24% to S$23.9 million.
The crane business drove the gains. Heavy Lift and Haulage external revenue grew 12% YoY, helped by Singapore, India and Brunei.
Gross margin widened to 40.7% from 37.6% on higher margins in that segment.
Turn to the cash flow statement, and you’ll see why Tiong Woon stands out.
Operating cash flow rose 31%, while capital expenditure nearly halved.
Free cash flow rose to S$43.7 million from S$6.3 million a year ago.
The board shared some of that cash.
It proposed a final dividend of S$0.025 per share, up 43% from S$0.0175.
You’ll still want to keep an eye on the balance sheet.
Tiong Woon held S$86.6 million in cash and bank deposits against S$108.0 million in borrowings, excluding lease liabilities.
The low capex bill may not last either. Management plans to keep renewing and expanding its fleet.
Demand looks supportive.
Tiong Woon cites official forecasts of Singapore construction demand of S$47 billion to S$53 billion in 2026, with Changi Airport Terminal 5 among the big projects.
Can Micro-Mechanics turn record profits into bigger dividends?
Micro-Mechanics (Holdings) Ltd
(SGX: 5DD) makes precision tools and parts used in semiconductor manufacturing.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (1QFY2027) ended 30 September 2026, revenue rose 45.0% YoY to S$24.2 million, an all-time quarterly high.
Net profit rose 102.8% to S$6.4 million, also a quarterly record.
Wondering why profit grew faster than sales?
Look at the margins.
Gross margin widened to a 20-quarter high of 55.0%, from 51.5% a year ago.
Overheads fell to 20.7% of revenue from 25.1%.
In other words, more of each extra dollar of sales now reaches the bottom line.
Free cash flow moved the other way.
It fell 10.6% YoY to S$3.7 million.
Trade receivables rose in line with higher revenue, and the company paid more tax.
Capital expenditure also rose to S$0.9 million from S$0.3 million.
Should that worry you? Not much.
Micro-Mechanics had S$33.3 million in cash and no bank borrowings as at 30 September 2026.
No dividend was declared for the quarter, and that is normal since the company typically declares dividends in the second and fourth quarters.
Spending is the bigger question.
Micro-Mechanics expects to invest S$12 million in FY2027, including expanding its manufacturing footprint.
Under a five-year strategy, it wants to double revenue to at least S$150 million. That investment will compete with dividends for cash.
What’s missing from Civmec’s record quarter?
Civmec Limited
(SGX: P9D) is an integrated construction and engineering services provider to the energy, resources, infrastructure, and marine and defence sectors.
It is headquartered in Henderson, Western Australia and reports in Australian dollars.
For the first quarter of the fiscal year ending 30 June 2027 (1QFY2027), revenue rose 70.2% YoY to a record A$324 million.
Net profit after tax climbed 75.2% to A$18.4 million.
A significant uplift in activity in Civmec’s construction division drove the growth.
Work ramped up on BHP’s Port Debottlenecking Project 2 and Iluka Resources’ Eneabba Rare Earths Refinery.
The order book stood at around A$1.4 billion, up from A$1.15 billion a year ago.
Here’s the thing: the quarterly update did not include a cash flow statement or balance sheet.
You can’t see free cash flow, cash or debt for the quarter.
For a contractor, profit and cash can drift apart as big projects ramp up, so this is a real gap.
You should also note how thin the margins are.
Civmec’s net profit margin was 5.7%, against 5.5% a year ago.
That leaves little room for error on large projects.
No dividend was declared for the quarter.
Civmec paid a final dividend of A$0.035 on 23 October 2026.
Together with the A$0.025 interim, that took FY2026 dividends to A$0.060.
Get Smart: Check whether the cash followed the profit
Free cash flow
is the lifeblood of dividends.
So when a company posts a big profit gain, ask one more question: did the cash show up too?
Tiong Woon passes that test.
Profit grew 24%, while free cash flow rose almost sevenfold.
Micro-Mechanics doubled its profit, but free cash flow dipped as it invested more and waited on customer payments.
Civmec hasn’t shown its cash yet.
So the next time a small cap reports a record, open the cash flow statement before you get excited.
Profit that never turns into cash shouldn’t count for much in your dividend plans.

title: 4 Singapore Stocks I Would Buy if I Had S$30,000 to Spare
article:
Every investor with cash sitting on the sidelines asks themselves the same question: If I had fresh capital in my account today, where would I deploy it?
With S$30,000 ready to work in the Singapore market, swinging for the fences on a single stock is a fast track to striking out.
The smarter move is building a resilient, cash-generating portfolio designed to
compound

From steady dividend powerhouses to defensive market anchors, here are four core Singapore stocks to turn S$30,000 into a balanced, wealth-building engine.
How I Would Think About Allocating S$30,000
Putting S$30,000 into a single stock is like putting all your eggs in one basket: exciting when it works, but painful when it cracks.
I’d start with a steady
dividend
giant and a defensive grocery stock.
Those two are like a safety net, generating cash and holding steady if things get rocky.
Then I’d pick a proven market leader and a company with potential for a strong comeback.
That way, I get the chance for real growth without taking a risk on my whole stack.
This approach transforms S$30,000 into a well-rounded, wealth-building portfolio that can keep growing year after year.
DBS Group Holdings Ltd (SGX: D05) — The Dividend Anchor
When building a cash-generating portfolio, every investor needs an undeniable core heavyweight.
DBS Group serves as the primary income engine, anchoring the portfolio with reliable payouts, high return on equity, and steady earnings visibility.
As Southeast Asia’s largest bank, DBS continues to deliver strong profits, driven by its expanding wealth management franchise, where assets under management reached a new high of S$544 billion in 3Q2026.
DBS offers a strong baseline annual dividend backed by its 9M2026 performance, where net profit reached a record S$8.82 billion.
On top of its S$0.66 ordinary quarterly dividend, DBS currently pays a S$0.15 quarterly capital return dividend, although this is a time-limited programme rather than permanent income.
Supported by a 39% cost-income ratio and a strong Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 15.9%, DBS is well placed to keep producing steady cash flow even when broader equity markets trade sideways.
Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX: S68), or SGX — The Structural Growth Leader
Building long-term wealth requires capturing secular trends, and SGX Group sits right at the center of Asia’s financial engine.
As Singapore’s main stock exchange, SGX operates an enviable regulatory moat with multi-asset expansion across currencies, commodities, and cash equities.
In FY2026, net revenue surged 13.9% to S$1.478 billion while adjusted net profit, which excludes one-off items, jumped 24.6% to S$759.5 million.
Reported net profit rose 7.8% to S$698.4 million.
Growth is driven by surging multi-asset volumes. Foreign exchange (FX) headline average daily volume expanded 33.1% to US$190.2 billion, while Securities Daily Average Value (SDAV) leapt 34.9% to S$1.8 billion.
Supported by government liquidity initiatives and high capital efficiency, SGX raised its regular dividend to S$0.445 per share and proposed a one-off S$0.125 additional dividend.
That would take total FY2026 dividends to S$0.57 per share, up from S$0.375 in FY2025.
Backed by guided medium-term revenue growth of 6% to 8%, a position in SGX delivers a high-margin compounding engine designed to expand capital over time.
Sheng Siong Group Ltd (SGX: OV8) — The Defensive Blue Chip
When market turbulence strikes, defensive blue chips steady the portfolio ship, and Sheng Siong Group stands out as a prime example of operational resilience.
As one of Singapore’s leading grocery chains, with 96 stores across Singapore and Kunming, China, its business model is anchored to everyday essentials that generate sticky, predictable demand through all economic cycles.
In 1H2026, revenue surged 11.9% year on year (YoY) to S$855.4 million, while net profit rose 11.9% to S$81.0 million, propelled by four new store openings and an expanded gross profit margin of 31.8%.
What sets Sheng Siong apart is its bulletproof balance sheet: the group has no bank borrowings and held S$402.3 million in cash as at 30 June 2026.
This fortress cash position supports an increased interim dividend of S$0.0375 per share, up from S$0.0320 a year prior.
An allocation in Sheng Siong adds steady income and defensive qualities to the portfolio.
SATS Ltd (SGX: S51) — The Opportunity Play
Rounding out the four picks, SATS Ltd adds real upside potential through its post-acquisition operational recovery.
After acquiring Worldwide Flight Services, SATS became a global aviation services group, operating over 225 stations across 27 countries.
That scale is starting to pay off as global air cargo volumes keep growing.
In 1QFY2027, group revenue expanded 11.3% YoY to S$1.68 billion, while net profit rose 6% to S$75.1 million.
Growth was fuelled by a 12.8% surge in Gateway Services revenue to S$1.33 billion, as cargo volumes handled rose 8.6%, outpacing the global market benchmark.
While near-term geopolitical costs and fuel prices keep margins under pressure, SATS continues securing new contract wins with major airlines like
Singapore Airlines
(SGX: C6L) and Air France-KLM.
For investors, SATS offers long-term earnings upside as its cash flows strengthen.
What I Would Avoid
Capital preservation matters just as much as growth.
Don’t put all your money into one sector, or you’ll leave yourself wide open to sudden industry shocks.
Also, don’t just follow the
hottest stocks
without digging into what those businesses actually do.
In the end, consistent discipline always outperforms quick thrills in investing.

Stick to companies with strong fundamentals, and give your investments time to grow.

title: Anthropic filing snafu jolts investors in run-up to mega IPO
article:
(Nov 10): Anthropic PBC is set to kick off the formal marketing of its blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) as early as Tuesday after an apparent snafu over the filing documents added a dose of last-minute drama to a nervous market.

Monday’s brief clerical misstep, in which a leaked prospectus mistakenly dangled a US$69.3 billion ($88.5 billion) fundraising target before getting retracted, provided an unexpected jolt to investors preparing for the Claude chatbot maker’s offering. The number, which the company reportedly later said was outdated, indicated a target that would fall short of an earlier goal of matching SpaceX’s record-setting debut.

Once the deal kicks off, Anthropic will be in a position to make the case to investors that now is the right time to go public despite last week’s swoon in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks. The gyrations of the past week briefly sent the Cboe Volatility Index, known as the fear gauge, above 25. That’s a zone in which companies typically postpone their IPOs, said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at IPO research firm Renaissance Capital.

Anthropic has little time to wait for the market to rediscover its love of AI, if its goal is to go public before the US Thanksgiving holiday on Nov 26. The size of Anthropic’s IPO and its investment case may put it in a different category from the average listing, Kennedy said.

“It’s such a big deal and such a unique asset that if the company wants to move forward, they can,” Kennedy said. “It just becomes a matter of where it prices.”

Anthropic will start marketing its IPO on Tuesday morning, IFR reported, citing people it didn’t identify. A spokesperson for Anthropic declined to comment.

See also: Anthropic IPO buyers see valuation as low as US$1.1 tril

The expected decision to move forward would keep the debate over its valuation target going, after some potential investors discussed a range of about US$1.1 trillion to US$1.3 trillion, Bloomberg News reported Friday. That’s well below where talks had been focused just a month before; in the interim, the Nasdaq 100 Index plunged 14%.

Against that backdrop of heightened market sensitivity adding to the valuation debate, Reuters reported that the company sent out and retracted a filing. Anthropic first sent bankers a copy of a document that indicated a sale of about 867 million shares in a price range of US$70 to US$80 per share, but then followed up with an email saying that those details were inaccurate, Reuters said. An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment on the errant filing.

See also: Dubai firm raises US$529 mil in UAE’s first IPO of the year

The retracted document was an updated prospectus sent by Anthropic’s outside counsel in Canada, The Information reported, citing people it didn’t identify. The counsel later told the banks that some of the details were inaccurate and it would update the filing later, it said.

Starting formal IPO marketing early this week, immediately following the end of a 15-day waiting period after last month’s public filing, would put the company on track to officially price the offering and debut on the Nasdaq Global Select Market the week of Nov 16.

The effort to win over institutional buyers will kick off immediately, with one-on-one and group meetings between management and investors around the world, either virtually or in person. Retail investors — who may get as much as 20% of the available shares, people familiar with the matter have said — will be tapped from the US to Japan to the UK.

Anthropic will need to quell worries about risks that have loomed larger as its IPO has progressed. Its quarterly revenue growth slowed at the end of the third quarter, and the data centers providing its computing power could be heading for a reckoning as a result of the Democrats’ success in the midterm elections — the trigger for last week’s stock sell-off.

Concern over AI safety is also increasing, and although Anthropic is a major proponent of slowing the development of the most advanced models, AI-sceptic Democrats may push interventions that differ from the company’s preferred solutions.

“Certainly buying shares in a company like this carries risks,” Kennedy said, “but there is also some risk in not owning a company that is disrupting so many other industries”.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Some loss of confidence in the AI trade is not surprising given the shift in political direction after last week’s US midterm election results, said Vivek Seth, chief executive officer of Shaires Holdings Ltd. The London-listed, AI-focused investment company backs Anthropic for its long-term fundamentals, he added.

“Anthropic is a once-in-a-generation company,” Seth said, citing its rapid growth, institutional backing and more than US$130 billion in cash and short-term investments. “Its IPO will establish a market-clearing valuation as conditions stabilise.”

Peter Singlehurst, the head of Baillie Gifford’s private companies team and manager of a fund that already owns a stake in Anthropic, echoed Seth’s praise, calling the company “exceptional” and touting its products’ potential to act more like a collaborator or team member, instead of just helping users work faster.

The biggest opportunity in AI may be in solving the hardest problems, rather than doing the greatest volume of work, Singlehurst explained.

“Some models are cheaper and perfectly good for routine tasks, but customers may pay substantially more for models that can reason better, tackle harder problems and work independently for longer,” he said.

Anthropic’s IPO filings left blank spaces indicating a potential price range, suggesting the company intends to give investors a way to signal their enthusiasm, or their indifference, through more than just their decision of whether to bid. That stands in contrast with SpaceX’s US$86.2 billion IPO in June, which came at a fixed price that left no wiggle room for negotiation with buyers.

Volatility in AI stocks during the marketing could play an outsize role in whether Anthropic investors lob in bids at the top of the range, after the sharp selloff left potential buyers nursing losses in their portfolios and less eager to take on exposure to new stocks, which are typically riskier. Still, some investors see greater risk to their annual returns from not participating in what could be the biggest IPO of all time, and being left behind.

“If Anthropic can take what it has achieved in coding into areas such as law, finance and medical research, where exceptional expertise is also highly valued, the opportunity is enormous,” Singlehurst said.

title: Energy security needs action on electrification — International Renewable Energy Agency
article:
(Nov 10): Wars and energy shocks are accelerating the case to electrify economies as governments seek to curb exposure to volatile fossil-fuel prices and limit imports.

Electricity is increasingly replacing fossil fuels in transport, heating and industry, and nations should aim to accelerate that shift, Francesco La Camera, director general of the International Renewable Energy Agency, said at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey.

A flagship ambition for the talks is to win commitments to increase electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from just over 20% today to 35% by 2035.

That is “exactly what we have to put into action to keep our promise alive,” La Camera said in an interview Monday. “If we don’t act, we cannot win the challenge of climate change.”

Electrification can reduce reliance on imported fuels, stabilise energy costs and strengthen economic resilience, La Camera said. “Everyone has realised that a centralised system based on fossil fuels is not good for energy security,” he said.

A series of meetings at the summit Tuesday were convening energy ministers, bankers and company executives on the electrification goal.

See also: China set to lead world in energy investment in 2026, CCTV says

“If you succeed in electrification, you’ll reduce dependency and you’ll fight climate change,” Turkey’s Deputy Energy and Natural Resources Minister Zafer Demircan said Monday. The summit host aims to lift electricity’s share of the nation’s final energy consumption to 36% by 2040 from about 22% currently.

Falling costs are strengthening the economic case for renewables, according to Irena. Since 2010, the levelised cost of electricity from solar PV has fallen by 89%, onshore wind by 71%, and offshore wind by 63%, the organisation said in a July report.

Disruption to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the Iran war has also added urgency to the deployment of renewables.

See also: India approves US$1.5 bil push for energy storage capacity

“We’re seeing more and more governments looking at what’s happening in the war and actually seeing that as a catalyst for them to really upscale renewables in their own country,” said Rebecca Williams, deputy CEO of the Global Wind Energy Council, an industry group.

More investment is needed to increase adoption of clean energy, particularly in offshore wind, where upfront costs are high, La Camera said.

Funding for renewables projects remains a constraint, according to Turkey’s Demircan. “The main thing is to find the financing,” he said.

title: New World’s top shareholder seeks bank loan as equity deal looms — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 10): Chow Tai Fook Enterprises Ltd, an investment arm of Hong Kong’s billionaire Cheng family, is seeking about HK$5 billion (US$637 million or $810 million) in fresh funding from banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

The financing would be a new-money loan and would be used for general corporate purposes, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private matters.

The fundraising would provide CTFE, New World Development Co’s largest shareholder, with a liquidity cushion if it decides to proceed with a broad recapitalisation of the cash-strapped builder. Such a move could include a rights issue, a mechanism where existing stockholders can buy new shares in proportion to their current holdings, other people familiar with the matter said last month.

The potential new loan for CTFE could be signed as soon as this month, though details are still under discussion, the people said.

CTFE and New World didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

The Chengs have been floating capital injection proposals for months as they explore options to support New World. That’s kept investors focused on how CTFE could raise cash to back any transaction.

See also: Hong Kong bourse operator's profit falls as AI scrutiny hits listings, trading

New World is still reeling from the property downturn in mainland China and Hong Kong and reported a HK$19.7 billion (US$2.5 billion) net loss for its latest fiscal year.

The builder has been seeking approval from its bank lenders to extend by two years about HK$88 billion in loans, which were secured in Hong Kong’s largest ever debt refinancing in 2025.

See also: Hong Kong chip IPOs tap intertwined networks of investors and bosses

The company plans to repay 10% of the loan principal using proceeds from the equity injection, which it aims to complete by January.

If a rights issue does go through, it would represent a major sign of direct financial backing from the controlling family for the debt-laden company. The developer has a market capitalisation of about HK$12.8 billion as of Nov 10, down 88% from its peak in 2019.

title: Vodafone raises profit forecast after cost cutting campaign
article:
(Nov 10): Vodafone Group Plc raised its full-year profit guidance after the British phone company cut costs and the size of its workforce.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation after leases will rise to €13.2 billion (US$14.8 billion) to €13.4 billion for the fiscal year ending in March, the company said in a statement on Tuesday. That compares to the €13 billion to €13.3 billion range Vodafone had forecast in July.

Chief executive officer Margherita Della Valle has been selling assets and reducing costs, which included cutting more than 3,000 jobs across Europe in the first half, to try to reignite growth at telecom company. Most of the company’s growth comes from less saturated markets in Africa and the Middle East, while its largest units in Europe face heavy competition for subscribers.

The company said it delivered €700 million in annual gross savings between 2023 and 2026 due to staff cuts and other measures. It expects to reduce European operating expenditures by over €200 million in the 2027 fiscal year and has announced 2,300 role reductions in Germany.

Vodafone’s shares closed at 116.95 pence on Monday and have gained 18% this year.

In the UK, the company combined with CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd’s rival business Three, taking the number of large mobile operators to three from four. Vodafone took full control of the venture earlier this year, and Della Valle said the merged business would save £1 billion ($1.3 billion) annually by 2032. The extra savings will come from shutting down overlapping sites and upgrading the two networks to be more efficient, the company said last month.

See also: Infineon boosts AI sales outlook due to data centre growth plans

The company is recovering from a 2024 law change in the German market that barred landlords from bundling rent with TV and broadband services, costing the company millions of customers. Vodafone is using broadband connections to differentiate from some competitors by selling bundles with mobile services.

title: Deeper economic slump tests Marcos, Philippine Central Bank
article:
(Nov 10): A surprise slowdown in the Philippine economy has triggered calls for the central bank to go easy on interest rate increases and for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr to do more to revive growth.

Economists from China Banking Corporation, Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co, Union Bank of the Philippines and Pantheon Macroeconomics have raised the possibility that the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas will pause its rate hikes after economic growth last quarter decelerated to the weakest since the pandemic.

“It sure doesn’t make much sense to slam hard on the brakes if we’re driving uphill on rocky terrain,” Metropolitan Bank chief economist Nicholas Mapa said.

Resurgent inflation due to the protracted Iran war and farm damage from monsoon rains have further strained the consumption-driven, import-dependent economy that is already falling behind most of its Southeast Asian neighbours. Household spending, a key economic pillar, remained tepid and weighed on a swathe of industries from retail to real estate.

Reacting to the poor data, Marcos’ office on Tuesday (Nov 10) said it is working to stabilise prices of basic goods and ensure a sufficient supply of food and fuel. “We are doing everything we can. The government is not neglecting its duties,” his press officer Claire Castro said at a briefing.

See also: Canada expands US tariff exemptions, cuts some aluminium relief

The central bank has said fiscal measures are expected to help the economy recover after it surprised markets with an outsized half-point increase last month. Governor Eli Remolona last week said the BSP remains in a tightening cycle as it fights persistent price pressures.

Inflation accelerated to a higher-than-expected 7.8% in October, well above its 3% target, and Remolona last week said it will take “a few more months” to peak.

The growth outlook for this quarter, meanwhile, remains gloomy, despite a typical consumption boost during the Christmas holidays. El Niño, which alters rainfall patterns and can fuel drought, is threatening to inflict more pain on the agriculture sector, which already suffered a record slump last quarter.

See also: Vietnam turns to taxes, state borrowing to finance growth push

“Looking ahead, economic growth is likely to remain subdued through the fourth quarter before recovering toward the 4%–5% range by the first quarter of 2027,” said Domini Velasquez, chief economist at Manila-based China Banking. “Demand conditions remain clearly weak, with a sizable negative output gap.”

But Bloomberg Economics and Bank of America said the BSP is likely to stay on course with its monetary tightening cycle despite weaker growth, with looming risks to inflation including El Niño.

Complicating any shift in the central bank’s tightening policy is the peso, which has declined almost 7% this year to be Asia’s second-worst-performing currency against the dollar. The peso strengthened 0.65% on Tuesday, recovering losses from the previous day and moving in line with gains in other regional currencies.

With weak economic growth constraining the central bank’s room for rate increases, the government “must do the heavy lifting", according to Jonathan Ravelas, a senior adviser at Reyes Tacandong & Co in Manila. Officials should, in particular, increase food supply by rebuilding local production to lower prices, he said.

The worsening economic slump has also prompted businesses to call on the Marcos administration to act. The Makati Business Club — which counts senior executives of the nation’s biggest companies as members — said the government should continue to restore business confidence and accelerate infrastructure projects.

“The policy response must go beyond stimulating economic activity and attracting investments,” MBC executive director Julia Abad said in a statement. “It must strengthen governance, institutions and policy execution.”

title: Infineon boosts AI sales outlook due to data centre growth plans
article:
(Nov 10): Infineon Technologies AG raised its 2027 data centre sales forecast, signalling confidence that the business will drive growth even as investor concerns mount over the artificial intelligence boom.

The German chipmaker sees data centre sales growing to around €4 billion (US$4.5 billion) in the year that ends in September, it said in a statement on Tuesday. Previously, Infineon forecast AI data centre power solutions would make €2.5 billion in the period. It also makes about €500 million annually from traditional data centres, and the new figure comprises both segments.

“We expect a significant increase in revenue and profitability in fiscal year 2027,” chief executive officer Jochen Hanebeck said in the statement, adding power chips for data centres and electromobility would be among the growth drivers.

Concerns about a possible AI bubble have driven a steep selloff in companies from chipmakers to so-called neoclouds. Infineon’s shares have declined by 45% from a peak in June. Demand for data centre chips has helped Infineon and peers such as STMicroelectronics NV compensate for slow revenue recovery from the struggling automotive sector.

Infineon is the only one among European chipmakers to give a full year forecast. The company tends to guide cautiously and then adjust estimates as visibility improves, according to JPMorgan analysts including Sandeep Deshpande. JPMorgan had expected Infineon to guide for 2027 data center revenue, including CPU and other non-AI accelerator-related power revenue, of between €3.5 billion and €4 billion.

As the buildout of data centers around the world accelerated, demand for Infineon’s chips to control power soared. Those chips can support advanced processors such as those from Nvidia Corp that are fuelling the AI boom.

See also: Zara owner backs new fund targeting supply chain emissions

However, a punishing post-US election selloff has rippled across the industry. Some potential investors in Anthropic PBC, which can begin formal marketing of its initial public offering as soon as Tuesday, discussed a valuation ranging from about US$1.1 trillion to US$1.3 trillion, well below where talks had been focused just a month ago, Bloomberg News reported last week.

Infineon’s fiscal 2026 revenue was €16.35 billion, matching analysts’ estimates, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The company sees sales growing to about €20 billion in the current year. The board will propose increasing the 2026 dividend by three cents to €0.38.

Infineon said its adjusted gross margin will be in the mid-to-high forties percentage range in the period and it plans investments of €3 billion to €3.5 billion. Adjusted gross margin was 43.1% in fiscal 2026.

See also: Vodacom profit jumps 26% as Safaricom gains boost earnings

The main areas of investment will be equipment for the ramp-up of production at Infineon’s Dresden site in Germany, the expansion of silicon carbide capacities in Malaysia, and the start of gallium nitride manufacturing on 300-millimetre wafers in the Austrian town of Villach.

Infineon is also considering setting up wafer fabrication in Thailand, although such a move is unlikely in the next three years. In September, Infineon announced it will sell parts of its memory business to focus on its core activities and more dynamic parts of its portfolio.

title: FWD Private issues US$318 million insurance policy
article:
On Nov 10, FWD Private (Bermuda) announced that it has achieved a new GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title for the most valuable life insurance policy. Valued at US$318 million (issued in Hong Kong), the policy issued by FWD Private provides a tailored, comprehensive solution that supports an individual customer’s wealth preservation and intergenerational legacy planning.

Established in 2023, FWD Private offers comprehensive legacy planning solutions and services for high-net-worth (HNW) and ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals.

Shelyne Shum, Chief Partnership Distribution Officer, FWD Private, said, "This record-breaking policy marks an important milestone for FWD and reflects the trust that HNW customers place in us. She added, "A case of this scale and complexity calls for tremendous collaboration. My heartfelt thanks go to our external partners, including broker adviser Charles Monat Associates, private bank and reinsurers, as well as internal teams across distribution, case management, product solutions, underwriting and corporate governance, for their dedication and collective effort in delivering this remarkable policy. Teddy Chu, Chief Executive Officer, Hong Kong, Charles Monat Associates, said, “We are incredibly proud to contribute to this new GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title of the most valuable life insurance policy for the second consecutive time, led by the same Charles Monat Associates consultant.
